# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Park should give a good reputation bonus

**Work item:** MS-0MVRDGNFU001DDQW · `feature` · `medium`
**Status:** Producer answers recorded (2026-10-28): **+20 reputation/turn, pricing maintained (150 / 40)** — ready for planning.

## Headline

The Park (`cs-park`) is the **only community space that yields no reputation per
turn**, while carrying the **highest running cost in the game** (40 coins/turn)
— it produces neither income nor reputation and the balance analysis records it
as a net drain. Give it the producer-confirmed **+20 reputation/turn**, keeping
its cost 150 and 40/turn running cost unchanged, restoring it as an attractive
tier-1 Entertainment anchor and the cheapest reputation entry in the game.

## Problem statement

The Park currently provides no value to the player. All seven other community
spaces generate `reputationPerTurn` (Playground 20, Garden 40, Fountain 40,
Library 40, Health Kiosk 60, Shelter 60, Public Art 80); the Park has an empty
`reputationPerTurn` (0) while costing 40 coins/turn to run — the highest
`ongoingCost` of any community space. `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md`
records it as a "pure net drain" (remedied by re-pricing 300 → 150 in
MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5, but the zero reputation remained). The producer decision
(2026-10-28) sets **+20 reputation/turn** with pricing kept at 150/40.

## Users

- **Player** — building an Entertainment cluster should feel rewarded: the Park
  is a tier-1, tutorial-visible card that currently reads as a money pit.
  *"As a player, I want the Park to grow my reputation, so that placing it is a
  strategic choice rather than an obvious mistake."*
- **Producer / balance owner** — confirmed the value and pricing on
  2026-10-28; wants the guardrails verified and the docs updated to match.
- **Developer** — a single-row, data-only change: the machinery that applies
  `reputationPerTurn` (per-turn income, tooltips, AI scoring) already exists and
  needs no engine changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-park` in `src/card-data.csv` gains `reputationPerTurn = 20`
   (producer-confirmed 2026-10-28; integer, no cost or `ongoingCost` change —
   remains 150 and 40). The description is updated with the existing wording
   convention used by Library/Garden/Fountain ("Provides +20 reputation per
   turn."), and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
2. **Value visible automatically** — the Park's card tooltip shows the +20
   rep/turn line, the per-turn reputation total includes it (existing
   `MainStreetEngineCommands` path), and UI/AI scoring that reads
   `reputationPerTurn` reflect the new value with no engine change.
3. **Retune-contract baseline updated deliberately** —
   `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts` pins `cs-park: 0`
   (`PRE_RETUNE_COMMUNITY_SPACE_REP`). This is the only card whose value
   changes outside the ×4 retune (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE), so the baseline entry
   and the test's rationale comment are updated with a pointer to this item
   (a deliberate, documented contract change, not a silent regression).
4. **Balance sanity** — the Monte Carlo / tutorial guardrails remain within
   band after the change (Park now contributes +20 passive reputation and looks
   more attractive to the AI's community-space scoring); any drift is measured
   and reported, and no band is silently widened.
5. **Documentation updated** — `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (Park row and its
   rationale line about "zero reputation and negative net value"),
   `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` (community-space table), and
   any other doc listing Park's rep/turn (e.g.
   `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` note) are updated to
   the confirmed +20 value.
6. **Regeneration** — CSV-derived static SVGs/checksum
   (`public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json`) are
   regenerated; card face text reflects the new description.
7. **Full project test suite passes with the new changes** (including any
   existing tests that assert Park has no reputation, e.g.
   `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` Park detail).

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** reputation per turn must be a whole number (20).
- **Balance levers only:** changes are limited to `card-data.csv`
   (`reputationPerTurn`) and description/docs; **no cost/ongoingCost change**
   (producer decision Q2 = maintain 150 / 40) and no engine-rule changes.
   Values are data-is-source-of-truth.
- **Do not break the win-rate ladder** `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` (primary balance
   gate).
- **No new cards, no scope creep:** `upg-garden` (Park → Garden upgrade),
   other card values, and AI heuristic changes are out of scope.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` `cs-park`: cost **150**, `baseIncome` 0, Entertainment,
  `ongoingCost` **40**, `reputationPerTurn` empty (0). Description: "Offers
  leisure space. Gains {SYNERGY_RATE} of base income per adjacent Entertainment
  business or community space. Costs 40 coins per turn to run."
- Current community-space reputation set (post-×4 retune,
  MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE): Playground 20 (300/ongoing 20), Garden 40 (350/10),
  Fountain 40 (350/25), Library 40 (400/25), Health Kiosk 60 (450/15),
  Shelter 60 (400/30), Public Art 80 (600/25). Park is the outlier at 0.
- Confirmed target (+20 rep, 150/40): rep per 100 coins of cost = 13.3 — inside
  the community-space band (Playground 6.7 … Shelter 15; Public Art/Kiosk 13.3),
  and still net-negative in coin-equivalent (−10 coins/turn at the documented
  1.5 coins/rep) — a deliberate producer choice: the Park is a cheap
  reputation-first card with the game's highest upkeep, not a coin earner.
- Test contracts that pin current Park values:
  `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts:66` (`'cs-park': 0`),
  `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` (Park tooltip),
  `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts:259`, `card-diagrams.test.ts`
  (Park detail), `community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (Park fixtures).

## Desired change

1. Set `cs-park.reputationPerTurn = 20` in `src/card-data.csv` and update the
   card description to state "Provides +20 reputation per turn." in the
   existing wording convention.
2. Keep `cost` 150 and `ongoingCost` 40 (producer decision Q2).
3. Update the docs tables and the retune-contract test baseline (deliberate
   change), and regenerate the CSV-derived card artefacts.

**Key Files:**

- `src/card-data.csv` — `cs-park` row: `reputationPerTurn` + description text.
- `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts` — `'cs-park': 0`
  baseline + rationale comment (deliberate contract change).
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — enforces
  data/description agreement for the "+20 reputation per turn" wording.
- `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` — Park diagram detail test.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts` — Park tooltip assertion.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` —
  Park fixtures/expectations may shift as AI now scores its reputation.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — Park cash-line fixture.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — Park
  ongoing-cost fixtures.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — balance gate
  evidencing the change (drift measured, not silently widened).
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — regenerates the
  CSV-derived SVG/checksum artefacts.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — Park row and its rationale line.
- `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` — community-space table.
- `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` — repricing note.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — Re-tune reputation sources (×4 retune) — left
  Park at 0 deliberately; the contract test that must be updated lives here.
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5** — Re-price community spaces — set Park cost 150
  "to reflect its zero reputation and negative net value"; this item removes
  that premise.
- **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL** — Per-turn running costs for Playground/Fountain/
  Shelter — established the producer-owned-value AC pattern and the
  description wording "Provides +N reputation per turn."
- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park 40/turn running cost (precedent).
- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE / CG-0MSKS963N000ZSTU** — Park-model synergy
  participation (unchanged by this item).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no engine change is required — `reputationPerTurn` already
  flows into per-turn reputation (`MainStreetEngineCommands`), tooltips,
  diagram detail and AI scoring, all derived from CSV. Verified by source scan.
- **Balance drift:** giving Park +20 reputation changes AI placement desirability
  and the passive-reputation economy; run the guardrails and report drift
  rather than widening bands (per the drift-report-then-ask workflow).
- **Value-by-design:** at +20 the Park stays net-negative in coin-equivalent
  (−10/turn) — the producer's deliberate choice of a reputation-first card with
  the highest upkeep; the AC4 balance gate confirms the ladder is unaffected.
- **Contract-test coupling:** the ×4-retune contract deliberately pins
  `cs-park: 0`; updating it is expected but must be deliberate and documented
  (AC3), otherwise a reviewer will read it as a regression.

# Competitive summary invariants and edge cases

## Goal

Harden the competitive Turn Summary end-to-end: only the seats the closing
actually surfaced get rows, every non-competitive and non-interactive path keeps
today's pacing byte-for-byte, and the gate provably adds no save, no state
mutation and no RNG consumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eliminated seats produce no row (no ghost rows): the panel renders exactly the seats the closing surfaced, and a test asserts row-count and row-identity against an engine run with one eliminated seat.
2. N = 1 and single-player closings never present the competitive panel; the existing single-player `shouldGateTurnSummary` behaviour (deferred only, skipping reduced motion / tutorial / replay / competitive) is unchanged and covered by its existing tests.

# Verification: remote pack precedence, gating & asset parity

## Goal

Prove that remote packs are indistinguishable from bundled packs at the
registry, gating and asset layers, and that precedence is deterministic, so the
parent's parity, precedence and asset-resolution criteria are evidenced by
automated tests.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2, 5 and 7).

## Scope

Verification-only: this item adds tests and fixtures; it does not add
production behaviour. Gaps found are reported on the sibling feature items.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Precedence — bundled wins.** A pack id present in both the bundled and a
   remote source is served from the bundled source, byte-for-byte.
2. **Precedence — remote first-wins.** Two remote sources carrying the same
   pack id resolve to the first-registered source's content.
3. **Registry composition.** The composed registry order is bundled first,
   then remote sources in configured URL order; registration is idempotent by
   id and never reorders existing sources.

   the bundled residential pack.

   the same active pack set and merged checksum after a load round-trip.

   URLs on the configured remote base, are gated on manifest verification, and
   reject traversal/undeclared asset paths.

# Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a signed pack catalogue hosted at a
configured URL to be discovered at runtime and merged into the player's card
pool, so that I can publish packs without rebuilding the game; as a player I
want those packs to show up in my Card Packs panel exactly like bundled packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1 and 6; parent scope items 1, 2, 6;
parent constraints "reuse existing seams", "totality", "additive", "signing key
separation"; locked decisions Q1 and Q2).

## Context

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts every layer once, end-to-end, so the whole
seam is proven before it is hardened. `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` already provides
`PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry` and adapts a registry to the loader's
`fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` seams, so **no core loader change**
is needed. The remote source is a provider on that registry.

Without this slice there is no usable increment: a signature gate is
inseparable from discovery (an unverified catalogue must never contribute
packs), so verification lands with the first end-to-end path rather than as a
separate layer.

## Scope

1. **Configuration surface.** Read the remote catalogue coordinates from
   `import.meta.env` (`VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL`,
   `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`), validate them, and derive the host
   allow-list. Inert when unset.
2. **Allow-listed bounded fetch primitive.** One total text-fetch helper: refuse
   a host that is not configured (before any request), enforce a hard timeout
   via `AbortController`, map every failure to `null` + one warning.
3. **Signed-manifest verification.** The signed envelope, its deterministic
   canonical payload bytes, pinned-key import from raw base64, and a total
   verifier returning a discriminated result (never throws).
4. **Remote pack source.** `createRemotePackSource(config)` serving
   `<base>/packs/manifest.json` and `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`
   after verification, rejecting the **whole source** on any verification or
   manifest-shape failure.
5. **Composition and boot wiring.** Compose the registry as bundled source
   first, then the remote source; use it on the browser boot path
   (`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) without touching the Electron
   content-directory path.

## Design notes

- Ed25519 is available natively in Node 22 WebCrypto and the Playwright
  Chromium used by the browser project — **no new runtime dependency**.
- Verification is memoised per source instance: one manifest fetch and one
  verification per boot, not one per CSV.
- The source's remit is "fetch and refuse only". Merging, precedence and
  duplicate-id rejection stay with the registry and the core merge, which is
  what makes bundled/remote parity automatic.
- Every failure is a warning on the existing logger seam; no UI change
  (decision Q3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` parses and validates `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY` (injectable env for tests) and exposes an allow-list predicate; unset, blank or invalid configuration yields no remote sources and logs a warning rather than throwing.
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` exports the signed envelope type and a deterministic canonical-payload function, plus `verifyPackManifestSignature(...)` returning `ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` / `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable` and never throwing for any input.
- [ ] A manifest signed with the matching private key verifies `ok`; a one-byte body change or a signature from a different keypair returns `invalid-signature`; a blank or absent signature returns `missing-signature`; a non-JSON or wrong-shape envelope returns `malformed-envelope`.
- [ ] The canonical payload is stable under input key reordering so an external operator can reproduce the signed bytes; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A total fetched-text helper refuses a non-configured host **without calling the injected `fetch`**, and maps timeout, rejection, non-2xx and body-read failure to `null` with one warning.
- [ ] A `createRemotePackSource(config)` factory returns a `PackSource` whose `id` distinguishes it from the bundled source, serving `manifest.json` and `<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv` from the configured base once the manifest verifies.
- [ ] A remote pack served by a fake transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merged pool with its cards and reaches the Card Packs listing input; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A missing, invalid, non-pinned-key or malformed manifest makes **every** path from that source resolve `null`, logs exactly one source-level warning, and never throws.
- [ ] The remote source never throws for any input (invalid config, non-string path, empty path, throwing transport), asserted by a table-driven test.
- [ ] `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` composes the configured remote source on the browser path, while an explicit launcher `contentDir` composes no remote source and performs no remote fetch (asserted with a spy).
- [ ] No new entry is added to `package.json` dependencies.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackFetch.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, composition
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — boot wiring on the browser path
- `./env.d.ts` — declared env vars
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDiscovery.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackIntegrity.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/remotePackFixtures.ts`

## Deliverables

- The end-to-end discovery path: configured URL → verified manifest → served
  CSV → merged pool → listing.
- The configuration, verifier and fetch primitives the later slices harden.
- Signed-manifest fixtures (keypair generation, signing, tampering, fake
  transport) reused by the verification items.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice.

# Remote pack degradation & bounded timeout hardening

## Goal

As a player, I want the game to always start and play on bundled packs when the
remote host is slow, hung, unreachable or serving rubbish, so that remote
hosting can never block boot or leave me with an empty Card Packs panel.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 3 and 4; parent scope items 5 and 7;
parent constraint "bounded timeout"; locked decision Q3).

## Context

The tracer bullet proves the happy path. This slice hardens the failure paths,
which is where the parent's risk register concentrates (boot latency, offline
regression). All of it is end-to-end observable: the game boots, bundled cards
deal, the listing is non-empty, and the console shows exactly one actionable
warning per rejected source.

## Scope

- Enforce the hard ≈3 s timeout on **every** remote request (manifest and each
  pack CSV), with the abort timer always cleared so no handle leaks.
- Degrade to bundled content — never throw, never blank the listing — for:
  unreachable host, connection rejection, non-2xx status, timeout abort,
  unparseable manifest JSON, wrong manifest schema/version, and a manifest
  entry with no readable `cards` file.
- Per-pack isolation: one unreadable CSV degrades only that pack, so other
  packs from the same source still load.
- Explicit "no client-side caching" behaviour: the source writes nothing to
  `localStorage` / Cache Storage and re-fetches on each boot.
- Warning quality: one warning per rejected source and one per failed pack,
  naming the source/pack and the reason.

## Design notes

- The timeout is per request, so a hung manifest does not consume the budget of
  every CSV read.
- Tests use injected `fetch` and fake timers throughout: no real network, no
  real 3-second waits.
- The bounded-timeout default (3000 ms) is a single exported constant so the
  documentation and the tests reference one value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
- [ ] A hard timeout (default 3000 ms, exported constant, overridable) is applied to every remote request and abort is enforced with `AbortController`; a fake-timer test asserts the default value and that a hung request resolves `null` at the deadline.
- [ ] The abort timer is cleared on every path (success, error, timeout), asserted with fake timers and a settled request so no dangling handle remains.
- [ ] An unreachable host, a rejected `fetch`, a non-2xx response, a timeout and an unparseable manifest each complete boot on bundled content with exactly one warning and no throw.
- [ ] A manifest with an unexpected schema or version, or listing a pack whose `cards` file is missing, is rejected whole with one warning.
- [ ] A single unreadable CSV resolves `null` for that pack only; another pack CSV from the same source still resolves and its cards still merge.
- [ ] A pack whose CSV header is wrong, or whose card ids duplicate an already-accepted pack, is rejected without affecting packs from other sources.
- [ ] The Card Packs listing input is non-empty when a bundled pack exists and the remote source fails (asserted by a test).
- [ ] A test asserts the remote path performs no `localStorage` or Cache Storage writes (no client-side caching this iteration).
- [ ] Warnings name the offending source and/or pack and the failure reason; asserted for each failure mode.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRemotePackFetch.ts`
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDegradation.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Bounded, leak-free timeout enforcement across every remote request.
- Total degradation across all availability and data-quality failure modes,
  with actionable warnings.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.

# Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack to never override bundled core content, and
deterministic behaviour when two remote catalogues offer the same pack, so that
remote hosting cannot silently replace or corrupt the game's own packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 5; parent scope items 2 and 3; parent
constraint "additive"; locked decision Q4).

## Context

`PackSourceRegistry` is first-wins by consultation order and `add()` never
reorders. Precedence is therefore *derived from composition order*. The tracer
bullet composed one remote source; this slice makes composition a first-class,
explicitly ordered function that supports several remote catalogues, and pins
the precedence guarantees with tests.

Equally important: the change must remain **inert** for the Electron
content-directory path and for an unconfigured build.

## Scope

- Compose several remote sources additively in configured URL order, always
  after the bundled source.
- Guarantee and test: bundled wins over remote (byte-for-byte); between remote
  sources the first registered wins.
- Idempotent, order-preserving composition; re-adding a duplicate source id is a
  no-op.
- Resilience: a remote source that cannot be constructed is skipped with a
  warning; bundled content still serves.
- Inertness: configuration unset, and the Electron content-directory path, both
  behave exactly as before (no remote source, no remote fetch).
- Gating is untouched — remote packs flow through the unchanged
  `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` resolver, so nothing is automatically
  ungated.

## Design notes

- Composition is a distinct, explicitly named entry point beside
  `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry`; the latter keeps its bundled-only meaning
  so existing callers and tests are unaffected.
- One place decides source order, mirroring the module's existing contract that
  "the registry is the single place source order is decided".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
- [ ] A composition function (e.g. `createConfiguredPackSourceRegistry(config)`) returns a registry whose `sources` order is exactly the bundled source followed by each configured remote source in configured URL order.
- [ ] `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry()` remains bundled-only; existing registry behaviour and tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] A test asserts bundled content wins when the bundled and a remote source both carry the same pack path (byte-for-byte comparison).
- [ ] A test asserts a pack id offered by two remote sources resolves to the first-registered source content.
- [ ] Composition is idempotent: composing twice, or adding a source with a duplicate id, creates no duplicate and reorders nothing.
- [ ] A remote source that throws during construction is skipped with a warning and the bundled source still serves content.
- [ ] With configuration unset, the browser boot path yields a result identical to the bundled-only build.
- [ ] With an explicit launcher `contentDir`, no remote source is composed and no remote fetch occurs (asserted with a spy `fetch`).
- [ ] A remote pack cards reach the applied pool through `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` when configured.
- [ ] An unentitled remote pack is reported `locked`; no ungating shortcut is introduced.

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `src/createMainStreetGame.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackPrecedence.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/PackSourceRegistry.test.ts`

- Ordered, multi-source composition with explicit precedence guarantees.
- Tests for precedence, idempotence, resilience and inertness.

# Remote pack asset resolution

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack's card art to render correctly, so that a
remote pack looks and plays exactly like a bundled pack.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 7; parent scope item 1; related work
`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` — pack assets self-contained).

## Context

`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` made pack art travel with the pack: the loader produces
`tce-packs://` asset URLs, `resolvePackFileUrl` maps them through the registry,
and pack art is registered from `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`. A bundled source
answers with a same-origin Vite `?url`; a remote source must answer with an
absolute URL on the configured remote base, and only for assets the verified
manifest declares.

This is a vertical slice: registry resolution → loader `assetUrls` → the pack
art registry → the rendered card texture.

## Scope

- Implement `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` on the remote source, returning
  `<base>/packs/<path>` for assets declared by the verified manifest.
- Gate resolution on successful manifest verification: a rejected source
  resolves no assets.
- Reject paths that escape the packs root (traversal) or are not declared by the
  manifest.
- Verify the resolved URL reaches `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` and the pack art
  registry so a remote pack's art is available before textures are generated.

## Design notes

- URL joining must respect a base URL with a path component (a catalogue may be
  hosted under a prefix) and must not double or drop slashes.
- The source returns a URL only; the existing asset-byte transport performs the
  fetch, so the remote source adds no new byte-reading path.
- No caching of asset URLs across boots (consistent with "no client-side
  caching this iteration").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
- [ ] The remote source implements `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` returning an absolute URL on the configured remote base for an asset declared by the verified manifest.
- [ ] A base URL carrying a path prefix (e.g. `https://host/packs-v2/`) is joined correctly; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A rejected source (failed signature or malformed manifest) resolves no asset URLs.
- [ ] An asset path not declared in the manifest, and a path containing `..` or a backslash traversal, resolves `null`.
- [ ] An integration test asserts a remote pack `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` entry is the remote absolute URL and that pack art registration receives it.
- [ ] A remote pack with art renders in the browser pack path, covered by an asset-resolution assertion or a browser test.
- [ ] The source does not add a new asset byte-read path; the existing `fetchAsset` transport still performs the read.

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `resolvePackFileUrl` on the remote source
- `src/MainStreetCardPackArt.ts` — pack art registration seam
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackAssets.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Remote asset URL resolution gated on manifest verification.
- Tests covering URL shape, prefix joining, gating and traversal rejection.

# Remote pack gating & behaviour parity

## Goal

As a player, I want remote packs to lock, purchase, enable, deal and persist
exactly like bundled packs, so that hosting a pack remotely changes where it
comes from and nothing else.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2 and 4; parent scope item 4).

## Context

Content-unlock gating is data-driven: `MAIN_STREET_CONTENT_UNLOCK_GATED_PACKS`
declares which packs are gated and `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` plugs into
the loader's `resolveEntitlement` seam. Remote packs must flow through that same
resolver unchanged — the remote source contributes *content*, never
*entitlement*. This slice proves that and covers the interactive flow end to
end.

## Scope

- Confirm an entitled remote pack loads and its cards merge; an unentitled
  remote pack is `locked` and contributes no rows.
- Confirm the scoped simulated purchase (`purchaseMainStreetCardPack`) unlocks a
  declared remote pack, re-discovers it with the same transports, and that the
  pack's cards then merge and deal.
- Confirm enable/disable parity (`applyEnabledMainStreetPacks`), including the
  refusal when a live card instance would be stranded.
- Confirm save/load round-trip parity: the active remote pack set and merged
  checksum are persisted and restored.
- Introduce no ungating shortcut: the remote source must not bypass or relax
  `resolveEntitlement`.

## Design notes

- The pack id a remote catalogue publishes is the entitlement key, exactly as
  for a bundled pack (`dlc:<gameId>:<packId>`). A remote pack that is not
  declared in the gating table keeps the default (Steam-DLC / declared-unlock)

- This slice is test-and-wiring only where the parity already holds; any real

- [ ] A test asserts the remote source never supplies or overrides an entitlement; gating remains owned by `composeContentUnlockEntitlement`.

# Documentation: remote pack hosting contract

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a written contract for hosting a remote pack
catalogue — where the files go, how the manifest is signed, what the game does
when it cannot verify or reach the host — so that I can publish packs without
reading the source code.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 8, parent scope item 8).

## Scope

- **Configuration** — `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`,
  that they are build-time (changing a URL requires a rebuild), and that
  multiple URLs compose in order.
- **Hosting layout** — the exact URL paths the game requests:
  `<base>/packs/manifest.json`, `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`,
  `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/assets/…`. A worked example tree is required.
- **Signing contract** — the signed envelope shape, the canonical payload bytes
  (including key ordering and whitespace rules), the algorithm (Ed25519) and
  the key separation rule: the private key is held by the operator and never
  shipped in the game. Include a worked example and the verification outcome
  table.
- **Degradation semantics** — the ≈3 s bounded timeout, console-warning-only
  degradation, bundled-wins precedence, no client-side caching, and that
  bundled packs remain the offline story.
- **Licence-clean requirement** — remote pack content must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs.

## Design notes

- Documentation-only slice: it consumes the contract implemented by the
  sibling feature items and must not introduce new behaviour.
- The verification outcome table must match the verifier's discriminated
  results exactly (`ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` /
  `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable`), so operators can map a console warning
  to a cause.
- Explicitly list the recorded follow-ups (signing tooling, client-side
  caching, runtime/launcher URL configuration) so operators know what is not
  in this iteration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
- [ ] `packs/README.md` documents the remote catalogue layout with a worked URL tree, and states that a hosted catalogue uses the same `manifest.json` shape as the bundled packs plus the signature.
- [ ] The signed-envelope shape and canonical payload rules are documented with a worked example an operator can reproduce, and every verifier failure reason is listed with its meaning.
- [ ] `./DEPLOYMENT.md` (or a linked page under `docs/`) documents `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`, the rebuild-to-change rule, and multiple-URL ordering.
- [ ] Degradation semantics are documented: about 3 s timeout, console warning only, bundled always wins, no UI change, no client-side caching.
- [ ] The signing key separation rule is stated: the private key never ships; only the public key is pinned at build time.
- [ ] The licence-clean requirement for remote pack content is stated.
- [ ] The out-of-scope follow-ups (signing tooling, caching, runtime URL configuration) are recorded as follow-ups, not documented as available.
- [ ] Existing documentation tests still pass and the new sections are reachable from the README.

## Key Files

- `packs/README.md`
- `./DEPLOYMENT.md`
- `./README.md`
- `docs/index.md`

## Deliverables

- The hosting contract documentation for distribution operators.
- A verification-outcome table mapping warnings to causes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.
- Depends on *Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence*.
- Depends on *Remote pack asset resolution*.

# Chart library integration spike

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 2, risk burn-down).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer on Main Street, I want proven, isolated Chart.js integration
with the Phaser 4 canvas so the end-of-game graphs can be built on a known-good
foundation instead of during layout work.

## Context

Producer decision Q3 = **B**: use an external charting library (e.g. Chart.js)
rather than hand-rolled `Graphics` or SVG-as-texture. Chart.js needs a canvas
context and a DOM element, and it must never load or run in replay / headless
(Monte-Carlo) runs. This spike de-risks that integration before five graphs are
laid out.

## Scope

- **In:** dependency addition, a thin `MainStreetStatsChart.ts` wrapper, one
  working overlay chart, headless/replay skip, teardown, bundle-size evidence
  and a documented spike verdict.
- **Out:** the five real graphs and column layout (third-column child), styling
  polish, docs prose (docs child).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dependency.** The chosen charting library (Chart.js preferred) is added to
   `dependencies` in `package.json` with the lockfile updated; `npm run build`
   is clean; the production bundle-size delta (before/after, kB and gzip) is
   recorded in a work-item comment.
2. **Wrapper exists and is Phaser-thin.** `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts`
   exposes a create/destroy pair (e.g. `createStatsChart(scene, geometry, spec)`
   → handle, `destroyStatsChart(handle)`) that renders **one line chart** into a
   dedicated DOM `<canvas>` positioned over the Phaser canvas at the requested
   overlay coordinates; the module has no game-state imports and no Phaser
   scene mutation.
3. **Headless/replay safe.** `createStatsChart` returns `null` and creates no
   DOM node when `scene.replayMode` is true or when no DOM is available
   (`typeof document === 'undefined'`); a unit test with a mocked chart
   constructor asserts zero constructions and zero nodes in both cases.
4. **Lazy-loaded.** The library is imported via a dynamic `import()` from the
   overlay path so headless/Monte-Carlo/replay entry points never resolve it;
   the existing engine/headless unit tests pass unchanged (changed-scope gate).
5. **No animation, clean teardown.** Charts are created with
   `animation: false` and no rAF/tween loop (reduced-motion safe); destroying
   the overlay removes every chart canvas — a browser test opens and closes the
   overlay 20 times and asserts zero leftover chart canvases and no console
   errors.
6. **Verdict recorded.** A work-item comment states: library + version, bundle
   delta, layering/positioning approach, teardown evidence, and whether the
   spike meets its thresholds (chart visible above the overlay panel at
   1280×720; gzip delta ≤ 150 kB; no leaks). If a threshold fails, the comment
   records the alternative approach and the item stops for producer review
   instead of continuing to the third-column child.

## Minimal implementation

1. `package.json` — add the charting dependency.
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — dynamic-import wrapper, skip guards,
   positioning over the Phaser canvas, `destroyStatsChart` teardown.
3. Temporary wiring in `showGameOverOverlay` to draw one series so the browser
   test can exercise the real path.
4. Tests: unit skip/no-leak test with a mocked library, browser open/close
   cycle test.
5. Bundle measurement + spike comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — charting dependency.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **new** wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — temporary single-chart wiring.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.test.ts` — **new** unit skip/no-leak tests.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.browser.test.ts` — **new** browser teardown
  test.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the capture/series-model child (needs `buildGameOverStatSeries`).
Blocks the third-column child.

## Deliverables

Dependency + wrapper + tests + spike verdict comment.

## Risks

- Chart.js may fight the Phaser canvas for pointer/depth ordering — the wrapper
  must own a separate DOM layer and stay non-interactive in this phase.
- Bundle growth — mitigated by the measured gzip threshold and dynamic import.

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 4).

## Goal (user story)

As a competitive Main Street player, I want the same end-of-game graphs for my
own seat so a loss against the AI can be diagnosed, and I want the overlay to
fit the viewport in both game modes.

## Scope

- **In:** competitive-series scope, both-mode rendering/fit verification,
  replay/headless guard verification, reduced-motion confirmation.
- **Out:** per-seat multi-series graphs (only if the producer overrides the
  recorded working assumption — that would be a separate item), docs prose.

## Working assumption (plan Open Question)

Competitive mode plots the **human seat's** trajectory only (see the parent's
Appendix "OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope)"). This child asserts
and documents that assumption; it must not expand to per-seat series without
producer confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive series.** With a competitive fixture (`players[]` populated),
   the rendered series equal the recorded `turnStatsHistory` for the human
   seat's closing values, and no AI seat's wallet leaks into the series (unit
   test asserting series points against a hand-built competitive history).
2. **Human-seat recording.** The competitive closing path records one history
   entry per turn from the seat-scoped closing wallet (`findHumanSeatId`
   semantics), never one entry per AI seat; a unit test drives a scripted
   competitive turn and asserts exactly one entry with the human seat's coins.

   chart canvas and no DOM node (unit test with a mocked scene asserting zero
   chart constructions), and headless Monte-Carlo/engine runs are unaffected
   (changed-scope tests green).

# Activate the committed git hook in this checkout; defer the full-suite gate to the engine

**Headline:** The producer has decided this game repo does the minimum now — repair hook activation in this checkout (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`), make the already-wired context-budget gate actually enforce by committing its thresholds file, and correct the docs that claim a pre-push full-suite gate exists. The full-suite gate and the reproducible scaffold wiring are deferred to a separate engine item (`CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`), so `dev` pushes from this repo remain full-suite-ungated until that lands.

discovered-from: MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O
related-engine-item: CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9

## Decisions (producer, 2026-11-03)

- **Q1 → (c) Defer the full-suite gate to a framework/engine change** that emits a game-repo variant resolving the global runner. This repo keeps the framework v2 hook content; it does **not** gain a test step here.
- **Q2 → (b) Only repair this checkout** (`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`); **no committed installer**. Activation stays a documented local step (accepted: a re-clone loses it until the engine item lands).
- **Q3 → (a) Game repo only**; the scaffold/`install_pi.sh` fix is a separate engine item — filed as **`CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`** in the Tableau-Card-Engine worklog.

## Problem statement

The framework documents the `pre-push` hook as the deterministic **dev-push integration gate** and `implement.py finish` deliberately defers full-suite testing to it, but this checkout contradicts that: `core.hooksPath` is unset, the active hook is the v2 variant with no test step, and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is absent so even the context-budget gate silently no-ops. Because `finish` defers the suite *and* the hook has no suite step, a red tree can be pushed to `dev` from this repo, and no gate-produced full-suite cache entry exists for the audit skill.

The producer's decision narrows the fix: make what already exists actually run here (activation + thresholds), stop the docs asserting a gate that does not exist, and track the real gate as engine work.

## Users / user stories

- As a **Main Street developer/agent**, I want the committed hook to be the hook git actually runs, so branch policy, context-budget regression and worklog sync apply to my pushes without per-session setup.
- As the **producer**, I want the docs to state the true current gate set for this repo, so nobody (human or agent) assumes a full-suite gate ran when it did not.
- As the **audit skill**, I want to know that no gate-produced full-suite evidence exists for game repos until `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9` lands, so it falls back to an explicit `/skill:test` run rather than trusting an absent cache entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Hook activation repaired and verified in this checkout (local, unversioned).** `git config core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`; `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to `<repo>/.githooks` from both the main checkout and a linked worktree; the resolved `pre-push` is the committed file and contains the branch-policy, context-budget and worklog-sync sections. *Metric: the commands and their output are recorded in an evidence comment; no installer or `.git/hooks` copy is committed (producer decision Q2=b).*
- **AC2 — Context-budget gate actually enforces.** `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is generated from this repo's current accepted startup surface and committed. *Metric: `measure_context.py --include-hidden --thresholds docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` exits 0; with a temporarily lowered budget the same command exits 2 and a simulated `dev` push through the committed hook is refused.*
- **AC3 — Docs state the true gate set.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` no longer claims the composition matrix uses a "pre-push/dev-push suite gate" for this repo; a short "Dev-push gate (current state)" note records that the v2 hook is active (branch policy + context budget + worklog sync), that `implement.py finish` still defers the full suite to a gate this repo does not have, and that the full-suite gate is tracked in `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`; `docs/dev/testing.md` cross-references the note and how to verify activation (`git config core.hooksPath`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`). *Metric: a reading of both docs shows no false claim, the actual gate list, the verification commands and the engine item id.*
- **AC4 — Engine follow-up filed and linked.** `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9` exists (engine store, `feature`, status open) covering the game-repo full-suite variant, scaffold wiring and `install_pi.sh` selection; this item links it as related work. *Metric: `wl show CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9` succeeds and this description cites it.*
- **AC5 — Full project test suite passes with the change.** The change is docs + a generated thresholds file, so no hook code and no new tests are expected; the full suite must still be green before the `dev` push (via `/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- **No full-suite step in this repo's hook** (Q1=c). Do not modify `.githooks/pre-push` beyond context-budget thresholds; the gate lands with `CG-0MW0KURL8002XOV9`.
- **No committed installer / no `.git/hooks` copy** (Q2=b). Activation is a one-line local `git config` recorded as evidence.
- **No edits inside `core/`** (engine-owned submodule). `core/docs/dev/context-budget.md` is read-only reference.
- **Do not weaken existing gates or bypass variables** when making the threshold file live.
- **Leave the dirty main checkout alone:** `git status` currently shows `M configs/engine-pin.json` and `M core` from another session; do not stage, revert or commit them.
- **Residual risk is accepted, not hidden:** until the engine item lands, this repo can push a red tree to `dev`. AC3 must say so explicitly in the docs; do not paper over it.

## Existing state (verified 2026-11-03)

- `git config --get core.hooksPath` → **unset**, so git uses `.git/hooks/`.
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` is present, executable and byte-identical to `.githooks/pre-push` (the seed's "absent" evidence is not reproducible). `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the shared main-checkout `.git/hooks` from linked worktrees too.

# Make `npm run scaffold` non-destructive: script wiring, regression guard, docs and engine pin bump

**Origin:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — _Scaffold generator: opt-in write gating and an explicit game-path migration flag_. That item's acceptance criteria 5 and 6 are carried over **verbatim** below (section "Acceptance Criteria"). They are delivered in **this** repository because the engine worktree cannot edit `tce-main-street` (worktree isolation), and because the engine generator change must land on the engine's `dev` branch before this repo can opt in.

## Why this exists

`npm run scaffold` here runs the engine-owned generator against the **live** checkout: it unconditionally overwrote `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, `env.d.ts` and `configs/game.json`, then applied a blanket `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` rewrite across `tests/` and `src/`. One observed run on a clean `dev` tree rewrote 11 files, including the drift guard's own `STALE_PREFIX` and 250 lines of documented LOCAL SURGICAL ADDITIONS in `vite.config.ts` (evidence: `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`).

The engine fix (producer decisions Q1=B, Q2=A, Q3=A, 2026-10-31) keeps today's default for fresh/extracted game repos and adds an **explicit opt-in**: `--only <file,...>`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, a machine-readable per-file classification report, and an opt-in `--migrate-game-paths` flag that gates the game-tree path rewrite (default off).

## Engine contract this item depends on

- `--only main.ts` restricts the run to `main.ts`: every other generated file is reported `skip-local` and left untouched, and **no** `core` symlink, shared-asset link, root app-icon link or path rewrite is performed.
- `--force` permits overwriting a **selected** file whose content differs from the template; without it a diverged selected file is `skip-local`. A full run (no `--only`) keeps today's behaviour, so extracted repos still receive template updates.
- `--dry-run` classifies and reports, writing nothing.
- `--migrate-game-paths` is opt-in; without it nothing under `tests/` or `src/` is modified. `--only` and `--migrate-game-paths` are mutually exclusive.
- Per-file classification vocabulary: `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Carried over verbatim from `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`:

- **Main-street consumer wiring.** In the `tce-main-street` checkout: `package.json`'s `scaffold` script passes `--only main.ts` (plus the flag name chosen in AC1); `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` copies this repo's `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, `env.d.ts`, `main.ts` and representative `tests/` files into a temporary directory, runs the scaffold against it and fails if any protected wiring file changes (while asserting `main.ts` is regenerated); `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` replaces the interim "classify-and-revert" rule with the new default and opt-in. All related documentation is updated (code comments in the generator explain why the overwrite is gated; any README or docs-site text describing the scaffold command is corrected).
- **Stability and validation.** `npm run scaffold` in `tce-main-street` twice in a row leaves `git status --porcelain` empty except for opted-in paths; the engine pin bump (gitlink + `configs/engine-pin.json` together) is a deliberate commit in `tce-main-street`; `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass there; the full project test suite passes.

Resolved interpretation of the AC1 placeholder (`--only main.ts` "plus the flag name chosen in AC1"): the `scaffold` script passes **`--only main.ts --force`** — `--only` limits the run to `main.ts`, `--force` permits regenerating it even when the checked-in `main.ts` has diverged from the current template.

## Minimal Implementation

- `package.json` → `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core --only main.ts --force"`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — temp-directory harness in the style of `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts`: copy the real `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, `env.d.ts`, `main.ts`, `configs/game.json` and representative `tests/` files (e.g. `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/docs-path-drift.test.ts`), run the generator with the repo's own script arguments against the copy, then assert every protected file is byte-identical and `main.ts` is regenerated; add a second assertion that a `--dry-run` invocation writes nothing.
- Engine pin bump: advance the `core` gitlink **and** `configs/engine-pin.json` together in one deliberate commit, pointing at the engine `dev` commit that carries the generator change.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — replace the interim "classify-and-revert" rule with the new default + opt-in contract and the reasoning; `docs/dev/testing.md` — correct the three passages that currently say `npm run scaffold` regenerates the `resolve.dedupe` and transcript-persist wiring (it now regenerates `main.ts` only, so wiring changes arrive by deliberate pin bump + `--force`); `AGENTS.md`/README scaffold references corrected if present.

**Key Files:**

- `./package.json` — scope the `scaffold` script to `--only main.ts --force`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — new regression guard (temp-copy harness).
- `configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink — pin bump travelling together.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — default + opt-in documented; interim rule removed.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — scaffold-regenerates-wiring claims corrected.
- `./main.ts` (plus `./vite.config.ts`, `./tsconfig.json`, `./index.html`, `./env.d.ts`) — protected inputs for the harness (must not be edited by a scaffold run).

## Dependencies

Blocked by the engine generator work (`CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` children) landing on the engine `dev` branch, because the pin bump must reference a real engine commit and `--only`/`--force` must exist in the pinned generator.

Scoped, non-destructive `npm run scaffold`; a temp-copy regression guard that fails if any protected wiring file changes; corrected docs; a deliberate engine pin bump commit; recorded evidence that a double run leaves `git status --porcelain` clean apart from opted-in paths, that `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass, and that the full project test suite passes.

### Sequencing & dependencies

- The blocker is **verified real**, not just asserted: the pinned generator (`core` @ `2c434518`, `configs/engine-pin.json` `2c434518f571880fb0ce51112006f2c90663c409`) contains none of `--only`, `--force`, `--dry-run` or `--migrate-game-paths`, and no engine commit carrying them is reachable from the pinned history. The item is therefore left `blocked` at `plan_complete` so `wl next` does not dispatch implementation against a generator that cannot honour the flags.

### Scope sizing

- No children and no phasing: one vertical slice (script wiring + regression guard + docs + pin bump) inside a single `bug` item. A `--only`-scoped run *is* the end-to-end slice — it exercises generator selection, the repo's script wiring and the guard together.

No new questions were asked in this session: the item was created from a fully specified parent plan (`CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`, producer decisions Q1=B, Q2=A, Q3=A on 2026-10-31, recorded on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`), its ACs are carried over verbatim, and the auto-complete path forbids re-litigating settled intent.

# Continue in solo mode

**Headline:** Solo play has exactly one automatic win target — the combined score threshold — and the producer has clarified that continuing solo does **not** involve choosing a target: switching to solo sets the player count to 1, so the target reverts to the value a solo game would have had from the start. This brief therefore narrows the engine change to that reset (the semantic already tracked by `MS-0MVWNXEX5006E7AT`) and records the brainstorm of *optional* new win conditions as a decision, with pros and cons.

## Problem statement

Solo play currently has a single win condition: `finalScore >= config.winThreshold` (`checkEndConditions`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` ~L880). All other `EndReason` members are losses (`bankruptcy`, `reputation_collapse`, `turn_exhaustion`), opt-in variants of the same threshold check (`turn_limit_victory`, only when `maxTurns` is configured — no default preset sets it), competitive-only (`last_standing`), or continuation markers (`score_threshold_continue`, `last_standing_continue`).

The original seed assumed a **target chooser** ("continue with a new target"). The producer has clarified that the player does not choose: in a multiplayer game the score target is the base threshold divided by the player count (human + AI, rounded to the nearest 50); when play switches to solo the player count becomes 1, so the target becomes the base solo threshold. The genuinely open question is therefore *not* "how does the player pick a target" but "should any new win conditions be added at all, and if so which".

## Users

- **Solo player** — "After winning, I want to keep playing; the target should be the normal solo target, not a target shrunk by the opponents I started with."
- **Producer / designer** — "I need to know the cost and value of each candidate win condition before committing to one."
- **Developer** — "I need the continuation behaviour specified without a new UI surface."

## Clarified behaviour (producer answers, 2026-11-03)

1. The player does **not** choose a target.
2. In multiplayer the score target is `winThreshold / playerCount` (human + AI counted), rounded to the nearest 50 — `effectiveWinThreshold` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` L59–62).
3. When switching to solo, `playerCount` becomes 1, so the target is the base threshold — exactly what a solo game would have had from the start.
4. `continueAfterLastStanding` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` ~L1197) and `continueAfterThreshold` (~L1227) resume play today but do **not** change `playerCount`, so the resumption keeps the competitively divided target.

## Brainstorm: candidate new win conditions (decision input)

Full pros/cons analysis is recorded in the work-item comment of 2026-11-03 (Q1 answer). Summary:

| Kind | Target | Headline value | Main cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reputation` | Reach a reputation target (preset-scaled) | Distinct axis; already tracked and calibrated (tier ladder 0 → ~4 000) | Same resource as the collapse loss; partly redundant with score |
| `challenge_sweep` | Complete N active challenges | Reuses the tracker with live progress | Conflicts with `MS-0MVAZH5OD000Q6E4` (no automatic all-challenges win); random draw varies difficulty |
| `complete_district` | Own ≥1 business of every synergy type (6) | Uses the breadth/synergy taxonomy; visible on the street | Card availability is tier/campaign-gated; six types are steep for a short run |
| `weekly_synergy` | Peak week synergy income ≥ target | Rewards adjacency engineering, the core mechanic | Needs new peak-week state; high variance and calibration cost |
| `full_street` | Fill all 10 street slots | Simple, visible, spatial | Effectively a coin-spending target; can stall |
| `upgrade_mastery` | Fully upgrade N businesses | Gives the upgrade economy a purpose | Gated by upgrade availability; partly coin-based |
| `liquidity` | Coins ≥ X **and** reputation ≥ Y | Balanced-economy goal | Closest to the existing score formula — largely redundant |

**Recommendation (assumption):** do not build a target chooser; if a new condition is wanted, start with `reputation` only, as a **solo-only, explicitly selected** target, so default runs and competitive play are unchanged. Record the remaining candidates as follow-up items rather than folding them into this run.

## Desired change

- **Settled part:** continuing to solo restores the solo target (`playerCount` → 1 / equivalent), deterministically and idempotently, without changing anything before the switch. This is the semantic already specified by `MS-0MVWNXEX5006E7AT` (blocking dependency); this item should defer to it rather than duplicate the implementation.
- **Decision part:** record the produced pros/cons analysis, adopt (or reject) a first new win condition, and — if adopted — create a dedicated follow-up work item with its own testable ACs, rather than implementing it inside this brief.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This item does not duplicate the continuation fix.** The continuation-target reset semantics are documented as owned by `MS-0MVWNXEX5006E7AT`; this item carries no competing implementation of `continueAfterLastStanding` / `continueAfterThreshold`. (Verification: dependency edge present; description cross-references it; no code change in this item.)
2. **Pros/cons analysis recorded.** Every candidate win condition has a documented value, measurable signal, cost and risk recorded on the item, and the producer decision is recorded (adopt / reject / defer per candidate). (Verification: analysis comment + Appendix entry present.)
3. **Decision traceability.** If any new win condition is adopted, a follow-up work item exists for it, linked as a child or `discovered-from`, with its own measurable ACs and an explicit "opt-in only" guard so default solo and competitive play are unchanged. (Verification: child/linked item present; guard stated in its ACs.)
4. **No behavioural regression.** Whatever the decision, default solo runs still win only on the score threshold and competitive play still uses `effectiveWinThreshold` unchanged. (Verification: existing engine/competitive suites green.)
5. **Documentation.** If any behaviour changes, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §7, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` and `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` are updated to match; otherwise the item records that no docs change is required and why.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No target chooser.** Per the producer, the player does not choose a target; do not add selection UI.
- **Player count is the lever.** The target derives from `playerCount` (`effectiveWinThreshold`); do not hard-code a second threshold source.
- **Solo-only new conditions.** Any adopted new win condition must not alter competitive play or default solo play; it is opt-in and explicitly selected.
- **Challenge-sweep restriction.** `MS-0MVAZH5OD000Q6E4` removed automatic all-challenges wins; any challenge target must be opt-in and must not resurrect that default.
- **Deterministic.** Evaluation is deterministic for a seed; no wall-clock or unseeded randomness.
- **Scope-creep guard.** At most one new condition is adopted in this run; the rest become follow-up items.

- `checkEndConditions` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` ~L880) — the single solo win branch; `checkCompetitiveEndConditions` (~L1390) — per-seat effective threshold.
- `updateScore` / `effectiveWinThreshold` / `computeScore` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`).
- `continueAfterLastStanding` (~L1197) and `continueAfterThreshold` (~L1227) — resume play without touching `playerCount`.
- `playerCount` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` L567) is number of players incl. human; set at competitive setup.
- Difficulty presets (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`): `winThreshold` 10 000 / 12 000 / 15 000, `endlessMode: false`, no `maxTurns`.
- Overlay continuation buttons (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` ~L434–475) driven by `endReason`; headlines in `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Challenges: `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES`, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN = 3` (`src/MainStreetChallenges.ts`).
- Synergy types: `SYNERGY_TYPE_NAMES` — Food, Culture, Commerce, Service, Entertainment, Health (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`).
