- `MS-0MUVQRCQJ00737UV` — Last-standing win + continue-solo option (completed; introduced `continueAfterLastStanding`).
- `MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4` — Competitive endless continuation beyond the win threshold (completed; `continueAfterThreshold`).
- `MS-0MTKQ8E5M0021WHW` — Endless mode button in end-game dialog (completed; overlay continuation pattern).
- `MS-0MVAZH5OD000Q6E4` — Completing all challenges is not a win condition (completed; constrains any challenge target).
- `MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE` / `MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D` — Competitive effective win threshold (completed; the player-count division being reused).
- `MS-0MV88T4I6000HQZG` — Tier reputation thresholds from Monte-Carlo ranges (completed; reputation-target calibration precedent).

- **Scope-creep risk:** seven candidate conditions; adopt at most one and link the rest as follow-ups.

# Intake Brief: Reduced income for duplicate businesses

**Work item:** MS-0MVYG50V1007W8BP · `feature` · `medium`

## Headline

Introduce a street-wide **market-saturation** rule: when two or more businesses
of the same type stand on the same street, each earns a reduced share of its
usual coin income — two-thirds with two copies, one-half with three, one-third
with four or more. Reputation is explicitly unaffected.

## Problem statement

The economy currently rewards placing many copies of the same high-value
business type. Beyond the existing *adjacent* same-type 60% base-income penalty
(and the nullification of same-type synergy), there is no cost to saturating a
street with one template. This mechanic adds a broader, street-scoped
diminishing return so duplicate businesses compete with each other, encouraging
a more varied high street without touching reputation.

## Users

- **Main Street player (single-player)** — wants sensible economic feedback
  when they over-invest in one business type.
  - "As a player, when I place a second bookshop, I expect both bookshops to
    earn less because they are competing for the same customers."
- **Competitive player** — needs the rule to apply consistently on the shared
  street.
- **Balance designer / producer** — needs a tunable, documented mechanic that
  the AI also understands and that the balance harness can measure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When exactly two businesses of the same base type are on the same street,
   each earns `roundInt(usualCoinIncome × 2/3)` for the income phase; three
   copies earn `roundInt(usualCoinIncome × 1/2)` each; four or more copies earn
   `roundInt(usualCoinIncome × 1/3)` each.
2. `usualCoinIncome` is the business's total coin income (base after the
   adjacent same-type 60% penalty, plus adjacency synergy); the duplicate
   factor and the existing 60% penalty stack multiplicatively.
3. Reputation is unchanged: base `reputationPerTurn`, `reputationBonus`, and
   synergy reputation are not reduced by the duplicate factor.
4. Every business card on the street counts toward its type's duplicate count,
   including sold businesses (a sold card still earns no income itself, but it
   still saturates its type). Community-space cards are excluded from both the
   count and the factor.
5. The factor is applied consistently by the single-player (`applyIncome` /
   `computeIncome`) and competitive (`applyCompetitiveIncome`) income paths, and
   is reflected in the cached `currentIncome` / displayed per-business income,
   the income-phase breakdown, and the sell-refund calculation.
6. Street scope is per 5×2 street cell; a 1×1 default game treats the whole
   board as one street. Duplicates on different streets do not interact.
7. Unit tests cover: two-copy 2/3, three-copy 1/2, four-plus-copy 1/3,
   non-adjacent duplicates, cross-street isolation, sold-business counting,
   community-space exclusion, reputation unchanged, multiplicative stacking with
   the 60% penalty, and the competitive shared-street count.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reputation (base and synergy) must not change.
- Reuse the existing `getBaseTypeId` "same type" convention.
- Every business on the street counts, including sold cards; sold cards still
  earn no income themselves.
- Community-space cards are excluded from the duplicate count and the factor.
- Must remain deterministic (no RNG).
- Integer economy: `roundInt`.
- Must not regress the existing adjacent same-type 60% penalty or the synergy
  rules; the two factors stack multiplicatively.
- The N=1 single-player path is the reference; competitive must mirror it.
- Income is computed per turn; an O(n) per-street count is acceptable.

## Existing state

- `computeBusinessIncome` / `computeIncome`:
  `totalIncome = effectiveBase + synergyBonus`, where
  `effectiveBase = (baseIncome + incomeBonus) × sameTypePenalty` (0.6 when
  adjacent to a same-type business) and synergy is a percentage of effective
  base per matching, different-type neighbour.
- `applyIncome` (single-player) and `applyCompetitiveIncome` (competitive)
  apply staff buffs and active-effect multipliers to each slot's cached
  `currentIncome`, then apply the reputation coin multiplier.
- `syncCardCurrentIncome` / `recalculateCard` refresh the cached
  `currentIncome`; `updateNeighborsOnPlacement/Sale/Close` already recalc every
  occupied slot, so a street-wide factor needs no new recalculation hooks.
- `getBaseTypeId` strips the copy suffix (`biz-bakery-0` → `biz-bakery`).
- Geometry: a street is a 5×2 cell (`STREET_COLS` × `STREET_ROWS` = 10 slots);
  the default board is 1×1 (the whole board is one street); expanded lattices
  tile street cells.
- No "duplicate" or market-saturation concept currently exists in the engine or
  the docs.

## Desired change

Add a duplicate-business income factor:

- Count every business card per base type per street, sold cards included.
- Resolve the factor from the count: 1 copy → 1, 2 copies → 2/3, 3 copies →
  1/2, 4+ copies → 1/3.
- Multiply the business's usual total coin income (base after the adjacent
  same-type 60% penalty, plus synergy) by the factor and round with `roundInt`.
- Apply it in the shared income computation so the cached value, the per-turn
  credit, the phase animation and the sell refund all agree.
- Keep reputation untouched.
- Add a named constant/configuration for the factor table and document the rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — duplicate factor in
  `computeBusinessIncome`, `computeIncome`, `applyIncome`,
  `applyCompetitiveIncome`, `syncCardCurrentIncome` / `recalculateCard`; expose
  the factor for the phase-breakdown base/synergy split.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyGeometry.ts` — street-cell scoping helper (or a
  shared `sameStreet` / street-index helper).
- `src/MainStreetCardsConstants.ts` — duplicate factor table constant.
- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — sell refund reads `currentIncome`; confirm it
  reflects the reduced value.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — income tooltip/description copy explaining
  the duplicate penalty.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts` — verify recalculation coverage (likely
  no change).
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — document the rule.
- `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/income-phase-data.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/competitive-income-events.test.ts` — new tests.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3` — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns (the
  current economy baseline).
- `MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE` — Re-tune reputation sources for the slower-coin
  economy (explicitly leaves reputation as the untouched axis here).
- `MS-0MUR9INHX001QCSE` — Synergy-diversity (G4/HHI) tracking; the outcome this
  mechanic is likely intended to improve.
- `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts` — existing same-type 60% penalty
  contract.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §Income (around lines 229–231).

## Assumptions (producer-confirmed)

1. "Same type" means the same base template id (`getBaseTypeId`), matching the
   existing same-type rules.
2. "Same street" means within one 5×2 street cell; the default 1×1 board is one
   street.
3. Only the `business` card family is affected; community-space cards are
   excluded.
4. **Every business card on the street counts toward the duplicate count,
   including sold businesses.** A sold card earns no income itself, so the
   factor does not change its zero income, but it still saturates its type for
   the other copies. (Corrected by the producer: the earlier "sold excluded"
   assumption was wrong.)
5. Competitive mode counts all same-type businesses on the shared street
   regardless of owner.
6. The factor applies to base + synergy; staff skill buffs and active-effect
   income multipliers then apply to the reduced amount.
7. Rounding uses `roundInt` (`Math.round`), consistent with the integer
   economy.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Balance swing:** the 4+ copy factor (1/3) is steep and stacks with the 60%
  adjacency penalty (effective 0.6 × 1/3 = 0.2 of base). *Mitigation:* the
  balance harness already measures economy pressure; re-baseline after
  implementation and adjust the factor table if needed.
- **Phase-breakdown drift:** reducing total income but not the synergy split
  would break the invariant that the phase sum equals the credited total.
  *Mitigation:* scale both the base and synergy components by the same factor
  and assert the invariant in tests.
- **Sell-refund surprise:** the refund formula reads `currentIncome`; a reduced
  value lowers the refund. *Mitigation:* document the behaviour and cover it
  with a test.
- **Scope creep:** the producer mentioned only businesses; do not extend the
  factor to community spaces, events or staff. Record any such opportunity as a
  linked work item.
- **Competitive fairness:** counting opponents' businesses can penalise a seat
  for another seat's choices. The producer confirmed the shared-street count;
  document it in the competitive rules.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1: what does "the usual number of coins" cover?

Does the factor apply to a business's total coin income (base + adjacency
synergy), only its base income, or its final credited amount including
staff/event multipliers?

- A) Total coin income (base + synergy).
- B) Base income only; synergy unaffected.
- C) Base + synergy + staff/event income modifiers.

**Answer (producer):** **A** — total coin income (base + adjacency synergy).

### Q2: how does it stack with the adjacent same-type 60% penalty?

- A) Stack multiplicatively (base × 0.6 × factor).
- B) Apply the harsher single factor only.
- C) The duplicate factor replaces the 60% penalty when both apply.

**Answer (producer):** **A** — stack multiplicatively.

### Q3: what happens with three or more copies?

- A) Flat 2/3 for every copy whenever 2+ exist.
- B) Progressive: 2 copies → 2/3, 3 copies → 1/2, 4+ → 1/3.
- C) Only copies after the first are reduced.

**Answer (producer):** **B** — progressive (2 copies → 2/3, 3 → 1/2, 4+ →
1/3).

### Assumptions 1–7

**Answer (producer):** Assumption 4 is incorrect — **all businesses are
included** (sold businesses count toward the duplicate count). The remaining
assumptions were not contested and stand as written.

### Follow-up note

The producer's "all businesses are included" is interpreted as: every business
card on the street (including sold cards) contributes to its type's count;
sold cards still earn no income themselves, so the factor only affects the
non-sold copies. Community-space cards remain excluded (assumption 3 was not
contested).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1** – Reputation bonuses should have no delay between businesses (completed)
- **MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW** – AI uses community space cards too much. (completed)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (completed)

- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptable, acceptance, active, add, adds (+278 more)
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: active, add, adds, adjacency, adjacent (+252 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: acceptance, active, add, adds, adjacency (+247 more)

## Answer to Q1 — yes, solo play has a single simple score target

Confirmed from the code, not the docs alone:

- `checkEndConditions` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` ~L880) has exactly **one** solo win branch: `finalScore >= config.winThreshold` (with the endless-mode opt-in variant of the *same* check).
- The other `EndReason` members are **not** additional solo win conditions: `bankruptcy` / `reputation_collapse` / `turn_exhaustion` are losses; `turn_limit_victory` only applies when a config explicitly sets `maxTurns` (no default preset does — `EASY_PRESET` / `MEDIUM_PRESET` / `HARD_PRESET` in `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`); `last_standing` is competitive-only; `score_threshold_continue` and `last_standing_continue` are the same threshold re-armed after a win.
- So the brainstorm is strictly **additive**: new win conditions do not exist today.

## Pros and cons of each candidate

Design cost shared by *every* new condition: new state + save compatibility, an end-check branch, game-over copy/progress UI, tests, docs, and a calibration pass. Solo-only conditions do **not** need AI work — both AI planning horizons (`aiPlanningHorizon` / `aiCompetitivePlanningHorizon`) are tied to `effectiveWinThreshold` and are competitive-only.

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **Keep score only (status quo)** | One understood, already-calibrated target (10k/12k/15k with Monte-Carlo guardrails); no new state/UI/migration; simplest to explain; AI and HUD unchanged. | Under-uses challenges, synergy types, upgrades and districts as goals; a continuation is just a longer grind to the same number; whole systems stay ornamental. |
| **Reputation target** | A genuinely different axis (community/Health cards, reputation synergy) rather than more coins; already tracked per seat (`resourceBank.reputation` / `PlayerRecord.reputation`); an existing calibrated ladder exists (tier thresholds 0 → ~4 000 from `src/MainStreetTiers.ts`, calibrated in `MS-0MV88T4I6000HQZG`); cheap to display. | Reputation is also the collapse loss condition, so the same resource both wins and loses; reputation is already a term in `finalScore`, so it is partly redundant; target calibration needs re-measurement after the reputation retune; risk of a one-note "buy reputation cards and coast" build. |
| **Challenge sweep** | Reuses the existing tracker with live progress; gives the challenge panel a win purpose; deterministic and easy to test; already per-seat credited in competitive. | Directly conflicts with the producer decision in `MS-0MVAZH5OD000Q6E4` (all-challenges must never be an automatic win); challenges are randomly selected (3 per run, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN`), so difficulty varies by draw; needs an explicit opt-in guard so it cannot resurrect the retired default win. |
| **Complete district** (≥1 business of each of the 6 synergy types) | Spatial/breadth goal that uses the six-type taxonomy (`SYNERGY_TYPE_NAMES`); rewards planning over stacking; visible on the 10-slot street; independent of score magnitude. | Card availability is tier/campaign-gated, so Health in particular may be unreachable in a run; six types may be too many for a short run; forces checklist purchases against a player's strategy; needs new type-coverage tracking + UI. |
| **Weekly synergy income target** | Rewards adjacency engineering — the core tableau mechanic; independent of hoarding; the signal already exists in the income phase (`IncomeResult.synergyBonus`). | Needs new "peak week" state and a week definition; highly sensitive to market/board luck; harder to explain and display; calibration is expensive (high Monte-Carlo variance). |
| **Full street (10/10 slots)** | Very simple and visible; uses the grid; deterministic "8/10" progress. | Largely a spending target in disguise (you need coins to fill slots); can be reached early and then stall; no interaction with reputation or synergy depth; trivial on Easy. |
| **Upgrade mastery (N fully upgraded)** | Gives the upgrade economy a win purpose; measurable (max-tier count); visible in the tableau. | Gated by upgrade availability in the card pool; upgrade costs are coin-based, so it is partly another coin target; "fully upgraded" needs a per-family definition. |
| **Liquidity (coins ≥ X and reputation ≥ Y)** | Rewards a balanced economy; two-dimensional, so it resists one-resource dumping; easy to display. | Closest to the existing `finalScore = coins + reputation + challengeBonus` formula, so largely redundant; two thresholds to calibrate; the pairing is arbitrary. |

## Recommendation

1. **Do not build a target chooser.** The producer has clarified the continuation target is simply the solo target (player count 1), which is the semantic already tracked by `MS-0MVWNXEX5006E7AT`; this item should not duplicate it.
2. **If new win conditions are wanted, start with `reputation` only** — cheapest, most distinct axis, already tracked and already calibrated via the tier ladder. Ship it as a **solo-only, explicitly selected** target so nothing changes in default runs and competitive play.
3. Record the remaining candidates as separate follow-up items rather than folding them into this run.

So the item's "suspected flake" framing was right about the trigger and wrong about the cause: it is a **deterministic load-sensitivity defect in the test**, not a scene regression. The full suite stayed green throughout because in-suite timing happened to fall inside the window.

### Cause

Both tests observed the HUD by polling the rendered text on a **fixed 14 s wall-clock window**:

```ts
const endOfSamples = t0 + 14_000;
while (Date.now() < endOfSamples && scene.incomeCollectionActive === true) { … }
```

Two clocks disagree under load. The income show is **scene-clock paced** (Phaser clamps each frame's delta), so on a CPU-starved host its phases land several times later in wall time than their nominal schedule; and the deferred HUD window is closed by a wall-clock cap (`INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`, 16 000 ms). At ≈1.3× CPU oversubscription the reputation phase began at 11.7 s of wall time against a 2.2 s nominal phase gap, so the grid-to-HUD collection landed *after* the 14 s window had already closed. The samples were therefore all `pre` values and a correct scene was reported as a regression.

### Fix

Observe the **production step** the HUD re-render hangs off, instead of racing the choreography on a timer. The reconciliation publishes every coin/pip arrival (and the final snap) through `scene.syncHudTotals`, so a recording wrapper captures the tick sequence at the arrivals themselves:

```ts
function recordHudTotalSteps(scene, kind) {
  const steps: number[] = [];
  const original = scene.syncHudTotals.bind(scene);
  scene.syncHudTotals = () => {
    original();                                    // behaviour preserved
    const value = kind === 'coin' ? scene.displayedCoins : scene.displayedReputation;
    if (typeof value === 'number') steps.push(value);
  };
  return steps;
}
```

The wait then becomes progress-driven with a **derived** budget (never a hand-guessed timeout), using the shared load-tolerant helper and the real production cap it races:

```ts
await waitForCondition(
  () => scene.endOfTurnDeltasApplied === true && coinSteps.some((v) => v !== pre),
  { capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS, floorMs: END_OF_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS,
    intervalMs: 100, label: 'coin total ticks at the HUD' },
);
```

A tick that lands after the old window would have closed is still recorded, and `post`/`postRep` are read only once `endOfTurnDeltasApplied` is true, so they are the authoritative final values. The per-file `waitForCondition` copy was replaced by the shared `@core-tests/helpers/waitForCondition` (which also keeps the triage-greppable timeout message shape). The reputation test additionally asserts every recorded tick is upward (`>= preRep`) — income is a gain.

The assertions still detect a real regression: if the count-up were removed the total would jump straight to its final value, `hasIntermediate` would be false, and the test would fail. Rendered-text coverage stays in the deterministic renderer tests (`main-street-renderer-deferred.browser.test.ts`, `hud-total-counting.test.ts`).

### Verification (three consecutive runs through the test skill)

```
run 1  success: true   29.5 s   failures: []      load average 10.5
run 2  success: true   28.1 s   failures: []      load average 10.5
run 3  success: true   31.9 s   failures: []      load average 14.6
```

Before the fix the same command failed 2/2 tests at load 19; after it, 3/3 runs are green at load 10–15, and the wall time dropped from 54.7 s (both tests timing out their windows) to ~30 s (both tests completing as soon as the choreography actually finishes).

### Documentation

`docs/dev/testing.md` gains a new section — *"Sampling during a choreography: observe the production step, not a wall-clock window"* — recording the two-clocks failure mode, the recording-wrapper pattern, the derived-budget wait, and where rendered-text assertions belong instead. AC2 is satisfied by that section.
